slides.title: Korea's market hit the brakes
body: Korea's main KOSPI index plunged **8.55%** to 4,923.47 on Friday morning, falling below 5,000, Newspim reports. At 9:03 a.m. Seoul time that triggered a **circuit breaker**, an automatic 20-minute trading halt.

slides.title: Samsung and SK hynix sank
body: Samsung Electronics fell **9.98%** and SK hynix, a Korean memory chipmaker, 11.71%. A sell sidecar, a shorter pause for program trading, hit the smaller KOSDAQ market too. On Thursday the KOSPI had already lost 5.28%.

slides.title: US chips' worst day since 2020
body: Hours earlier, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell **12.3%**, its worst day since March 2020, NBC News reports. The Nasdaq Composite lost 5.5% and the Dow fell 1,833 points.

slides.title: The midterms spooked investors
body: In this week's US midterms, Democrats took **control of both chambers** of Congress, Korea JoongAng Daily reports. Investors fear tougher regulation of AI data centers, the facilities that run AI and buy these chips.

slides.title: 45% of new capacity at risk
body: According to Goldman Sachs, **45%** of planned new data center capacity could be at risk, Korea JoongAng Daily reports. These are Friday morning numbers, not the close.

facts.text: KOSPI fell 460.33 points (8.55%) to 4,923.47 on the morning of Nov 6, falling below the 5,000 line.
A circuit breaker (level 1) was triggered at 9:03 a.m.; trading stopped for 20 minutes.
Samsung Electronics fell 9.98% to 181,400 won; SK hynix fell 11.71%.
A sell sidecar was triggered on the KOSDAQ market.
The previous day (Nov 5) the KOSPI fell 5.28% to 5,383.80.
On Thursday (Nov 5) the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 12.3%, its worst day since March 2020. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5%; the Dow Jones fell 1,833 points.
Democrats took control of both chambers of Congress in the US midterms.
Goldman Sachs: 45 percent of planned new capacity could be at risk.

Korea's KOSPI just plunged 8.55% and tripped a circuit breaker, halting all trading for 20 minutes.

→ The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had its worst day since March 2020 (-12.3%), NBC News reports
